BURHAN:v3p293/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p293/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p293/r9.claim: The author says إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم is God's speech, while إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم belongs to Abraham's speech.
BURHAN:v3p293/r9.anchor: وقوله ﴿ إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم ﴾ 3 من كلامه تعالى وقال ﴿ إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم ﴾ 4

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r4.speaker: İbn Kesîr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r4.claim: One gloss of a sound heart is a heart free of polytheism and doubt, sincerely believing the articles of faith and spiritually healthy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r4.anchor: şirk ve şüpheden arınmış, iman esaslarına samimiyetle inanmış, mânen sağlıklı (İbn Kesîr, VI, 159)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r5.speaker: Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r5.claim: Asad glosses a sound heart as one protected from evils.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r5.anchor: mânen sağlıklı (İbn Kesîr, VI, 159), kötülüklerden korunmuş (Esed, II, 749)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r6.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r6.claim: Another gloss describes a sound heart as devoted to the Sunnah, free of innovations, and not made arrogant by wealth or children.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r6.anchor: sünnete gönülden bağlı olup bid‘atlardan uzak duran, mal ve evlât sahibi olduğu için şımarmayan bir kalp (Şevkânî, IV, 103).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r7.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r7.claim: Razi prefers the definition of a sound heart as one purified of ignorance and bad character.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r7.anchor: Râzî’ye göre bu konudaki görüşlerin en doğrusu, kalb-i selîmi, “Cehaletten ve kötü huylardan arınmış kalptir” diye tanımlayan görüştür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.claim: Exegetes cite various proofs that all of Abraham's requests were granted except his prayer concerning his father.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:26:83/r10.anchor: Müfessirler, İbrâhim’in babasının affı dışındaki bütün dileklerinin kabul olunduğuna dair çeşitli deliller getirmişlerdir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.claim: The exception about the sound-hearted is God’s own completion and explanation of Abraham’s prayer; if a child could benefit his parent, Azar would have benefited from having Abraham as a son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r2.anchor: These words are not part of Abraham’s prayer. They are in fact from God Himself and complete and explain the prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r3.claim: A pure heart is wholly free of polytheism and hypocrisy; a heart afflicted by them has no weight before God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p424/r3.anchor: The expression “pure heart” refers to a heart that is completely devoid of any speck of polytheism and hypocrisy.

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r2.claim: The exception means that only a sincere person with a heart sound from disbelief and hypocrisy benefits; faith is required for either wealth or children to help.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r2.anchor: {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} بدل من مفعوله المحذوف أي إلا مخلصا سليم القلب

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r3.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r3.claim: Kashf al-Asrār says a sound heart is safe from disbelief and sins; the heart is named because the limbs follow its health or corruption, as in the report about the heart being a morsel of flesh.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r3.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : بنفس سليمة من الكفر والمعاصي وإنما أضافه إلى القلب لأن الجوارح

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.speaker: ليث
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.claim: Al-Layth says disbelievers boasted of wealth and children, but these cannot help without sound hearts; Muslims benefit from good deeds and from righteous children, whether the child dies first or later prays for the parent.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r4.anchor: قال الليث : كان الكفار يقولون : نحن أكثر أموالا وأولادا

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r5.speaker: أبو القاسم الحكيم
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r5.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Ḥakīm lists three signs of a sound heart: harming no one, not nursing hurt from anyone, and expecting no repayment for kindness; these show piety, loyalty, and sincerity.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r5.anchor: وسئل أبو القاسم الحكيم عن القلب السليم فقال : له ثلاث علامات أولاها : أن لا يؤذي أحدا

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r6.claim: Al-Kāshifī reports that soundness is sincerity in the testimony of faith; he also says a sound heart is free of worldly love, while others say it is free of envy and betrayal.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r6.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (كفته اند سلامت قلب إخلاص است

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r7.speaker: تيسير
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r7.claim: A reading in Taysīr defines the sound heart as free from hatred of the Prophet's family, wives, and Companions.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r7.anchor: ودرتيسير كويد از بغض أهل بيت وازواج وأصحاب حضرت يغمبر عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r8.speaker: قشيري
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r8.claim: Al-Qushayrī says a sound heart is empty of all besides God, worldly greed, and hope for the afterlife; another reported reading says it is free of innovation and settled upon the Sunnah.
BURSEVI:v6p208#3/r8.anchor: إمام قشيري رحمه الله فرمودكه قلب سليم آنست كه خالي باشد ازغير خداي ازطمع دنيا ورجاء عقبى يا خالي باشد از بدعت ومطمن بسنت

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r1.speaker: جنيد
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r1.claim: Junayd says salīm means bitten by a snake; one bitten remains anxious and agitated, suggesting the sound heart's constant fear of separation or longing for union.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r1.anchor: واز سيد ذطائفة جنيد قدس سره منقولست كه سليم ماركزيده بود وماركزيده يوسته درقلق واضطرابست س بيان ميكند كه دل سليم مدام درمقام جزع وتضرع

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r2.claim: The cited poetry describes the pain of nearness as greater than distance, with closeness bringing fear of loss and distance offering hope of reunion.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r2.anchor: قال المولى الجامي : محنت قرب ز بعد افزونست جكر از محنت مرهم خونست

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r4.speaker: بحر
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r4.claim: Baḥr reads coming to God as arrival at the moment of watchfulness, with a sound heart free of the original distortion of created nature; the heart was created as a mirror for divine attributes before worldly attachments tarnished it.

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r5.speaker: بحر
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r5.claim: Baḥr says the exception points to taking on God's character and attributes: the heart is sound when it embodies sacred purity rather than looking toward creation.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r5.anchor: أشار بقوله : {إلا من} إلى التخلق بخلق الله والاتصاف بصفته

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ defines the sound heart as one untroubled by any affliction of the created world.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : السليم الذي لا يشوشه شيء من آفات الكون

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r7.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r7.claim: One person says serenity of the breast comes from observing the limits of certainty and abandoning personal will amid changing or established states.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r7.anchor: وسئل بعضهم : بم تنال سلامة الصدر؟ قال : بالوقوف على حد اليقين

BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r8.speaker: أبو يزيد
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r8.claim: Abū Yazīd recounts traveling through deserts, the spiritual world, and the angelic realm; offered all he had seen, he asked instead to want nothing, and was granted that state.
BURSEVI:v6p208#4/r8.anchor: قال أبو يزيد رحمه الله : فقطعت المفاوز حتى بلغت البوادي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74#3/r1.claim: Qatadah says a sound heart is one free of shirk.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p74#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ بقلب سليم ﴾ قال سليم من الشرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r9.claim: The apparent syntax is a disconnected exception: rather, the person who comes to God with a sound heart benefits from that soundness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r9.anchor: والظاهر أن الاستثناء منقطع، أي لكن من أتى الله بقلب سليم ينفعه سلامة قلبه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the disconnected exception requires an implied noun meaning the state of soundness, since that state is not the same category as wealth and sons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ولك أن تجعل الاستثناء منقطعا، ولا بد لك مع ذلك من تقدير المضاف، وهو الحال المراد بها السلامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r11.claim: The author sees no need to supply an omitted noun: the meaning is simply that the one arriving with a sound heart benefits from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r11.anchor: ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى حذف مضاف، كما ذكر، إذ قدرناه، لكن من أتى الله بقلب سليم ينفعه ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also offers a connected reading, taking the exception as the state of the person who comes to God with a sound heart; the discussion continues with rhetorical illustrations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p168/r12.anchor: وقد جعله الزمخشري في أول توجيهه متصلا بتأويل قال: إلا من أتى الله: إلا حال من أتى الله بقلب سليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī illustrates the connected exception as substituting a sound heart for wealth and sons, or reads wealth figuratively as religious prosperity found in the person with a sound heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r1.anchor: ومثاله أن يقال: هل لزيد مال وبنون؟ فيقول: ماله وبنوه سلامة قلبه، تريد نفي المال والبنين عنه، وإثبات سلامة القلب له بدلا عن ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r2.claim: Some parse the exception as a free object of ينفع: wealth spent in good and righteous children taught religion benefit the person who comes with a sound heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r2.anchor: وجعله بعضهم استثناء مفرغا، فمن مفعول، والتقدير: لا ينفع مال ولا بنون أحدا إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r3.claim: سلامة القلب means freedom from shirk, sins, and attachment to worldly things, even when those things are permissible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r3.anchor: وسلامة القلب، خلوصه من الشرك والمعاصي، وعلق الدنيا المتروكة وإن كانت مباحة كالمال والبنين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r4.speaker: سفيان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r4.claim: Sufyān says a sound heart is one that meets its Lord with nothing in it besides Him; the wording supports this breadth, but freedom from shirk is broader.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r4.anchor: وقال سفيان: هو الذي يلقى ربه وليس في قلبه شيء غيره، وهذا يقتضي عمومه اللفظ، ولكن السليم من الشرك هو الأعم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r5.speaker: الجنيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r5.claim: Al-Junayd interprets it as a heart wounded by fear of God, taking سليم to mean bitten or stung.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r5.anchor: وقال الجنيد: بقلب لديغ من خشية الله، والسليم: اللديغ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls al-Junayd’s interpretation an invented exegesis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p169/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هو من بدع التفاسير وصدق.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.claim: The apparent reading makes all these clauses part of Abraham's speech, reporting what God taught him about his people and the Resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الجمل كلها متعلقة بقول إبراهيم، أخبر بما أعلمه الله من أحوال يوم القيامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya separates “the day when wealth and children do not benefit” from Abraham's speech, treating it as God's description of the Day Abraham feared being disgraced on.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p171/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وهذه الآيات من قوله: يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون هي عندي منقطعة من كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r1.claim: One parsing makes the exception apply to the general objects of نفع, with من accusative: neither charity-spent wealth nor righteous sons deserving intercession help, except for the sound-hearted believer.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r1.anchor: استثناء من أعم المفاعيل و ( من ) محل نصب أي يوم لاينفع مال

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r2.claim: A sound heart is free from intellectual illness and hypocrisy, since benefit from wealth and children requires faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r2.anchor: إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم عن مرض الفكر والنفاق ضرورة اشتراط نفع كل منهما بالايمان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r3.claim: This supports reading Abraham's prayer for his father as guidance to faith: forgiveness after his father's death as an unbeliever would be futile intercession.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r3.anchor: وفي هذا تأييد لكون استغفاره عليه السلام لابيه طلبا لهدايته إلى الايمان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, the exception is from the subject of ينفع, and من is nominative; with an implied noun, only the wealth and children of a sound-hearted person benefit through charity and good upbringing.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو استثناء من فاعل ( ينفع ) ومن في محل رفع بدل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r5.claim: A third parsing makes the exception from the implied general meaning of wealth and children: only the spiritual wealth of a sound heart benefits.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : هو استثناء مما دل عليه المال والبنون دلالة الخاص على العام أعني مطلق الغنى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r1.speaker: ثوبان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r1.claim: Thawban reports that after the verse on hoarding gold and silver was revealed, the Prophet named a remembering tongue, grateful heart, and righteous faith-supporting spouse as the best wealth.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r1.anchor: أخرج أحمد والترمذي وابن ماجة عن ثوبان قال : لما نزلت ( والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ) الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r2.claim: He treats the exception as disconnected from مال and requires an omitted noun, such as حال, for it to make sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ولابد من تقدير المضاف ولو لم يقدر لم يحصل للاستثناء معنى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that the meaning works without ellipsis if the exception means that the sound-hearted person will be safe or benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r3.anchor: ومنع ذلك أبو حيان بانه لو قدر مثلا لكن من أتى الله بقلب سليم يسلم أو ينتفع يستقيم المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r4.claim: Al-Kashf replies that as an exception from wealth the meaning requires an omitted noun; Abu Hayyan's alternative shifts to the whole sentence and misses that issue.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r4.anchor: وأجاب عنه في الكشف بأن المراد أنه على طريق الاستثناء من مال لايتحصل المعنى بدون تقدير المضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r5.claim: An exception connected through an implied condition is also permitted; the author illustrates it with a saying in which a greeting is a painful blow.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r5.anchor: وقد جوز أتصال الاستثناء بتقدير الحال على جعل الكلام من باب + تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع +

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r6.claim: One may deny wealth and sons while naming soundness of heart as their substitute, as in the example about Zayd.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r6.anchor: ومثاله أن يقال : هل لزيد مال وبنون فتقول ماله وبنوه سلامة قلبه تريد نفي المال والبنين عنه وإثبات سلامة القلب بدلا عن ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وابن سيرين وغيرهم
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r7.claim: The transmitted interpretation is a heart free from the disease of disbelief and hypocrisy; the author says this best suits the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r7.anchor: وكون المراد من القلب السليم القلب السليم عن مرض الكفر والنفاق هو المأثور عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وابن سيرين وغيرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r8.claim: The Imam defines it as freedom from false beliefs and worldly desires; righteous deeds follow because soundness of heart affects the limbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r8.anchor: وقال الامام : هو الخالي عن العقائد الفاسدة والميل إلى شهوات الدنيا ولذاتها

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r9.speaker: سفيان
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r9.claim: Sufyan says the sound heart contains nothing besides God.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r9.anchor: وقال سفيان : هو الذي ليس فيه غير الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r10.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r10.claim: Junayd describes it as stung by fear of God, anxious and shaken by fear of separation; Arabic also uses سليم for someone bitten by a snake.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r10.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره : هو اللديغ من خشية الله تعالى القلق المنزعج من مخافة القطيعة وشاع إطلاق السليم في لسان العرب على اللديغ

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r11.claim: Another interpretation is a heart free of shirk and sins, surrendered to God's judgment, loyal to His allies, opposed to His enemies, and obedient in worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r11.anchor: وقيل : هو الذي سلم من الشرك والمعاصي وسلم نفسه لحكم الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r12.claim: The transmitted meaning best fits the context; al-Zamakhshari calls the mystical readings beginning with Junayd innovations, and Abu Hayyan agrees regarding the first.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p100#4/r12.anchor: والأنسب بالمقام المعنى المأثور وما ذ : ره من تأويلات الصوفية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r4.claim: He says the sound heart is healthy: the believer’s heart is sound, while the disbeliever’s and hypocrite’s hearts are sick.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: القلب السليم هو الصحيح، وهو قلب المؤمن لأن قلب الكافر والمنافق مريض.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r5.speaker: ابن عثمان النيسابوري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r5.claim: He defines the sound heart as free of innovation and settled upon the Sunnah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p119/r5.anchor: هو القلب الخالي من البدعة المطمئن على السنة

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r1.claim: A sound heart is free from every preoccupation except its Lord, with an unobstructed path to Him and no joy in anything besides Him.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : قلب خال من الاشتغال بشيء سوى مولاه

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r2.claim: One lexical reading takes salim to mean stung: like a restless, anguished person, the heart remains unsettled in grief and supplication over separation.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : السليم في لسان العرب اللديغ ، واللديغ هو القلق المزعج

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r3.claim: One definition of a sound heart is that it is safe from an evil decree.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : سلم من سوء القضاء

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r4.claim: When asked what a sound heart is, Wāsiṭī answered that it is free from turning away from God.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r4.anchor: وسئل الواسطي عن القلب السليم ؟ فقال : سليم من الإعراض عن الله

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r5.claim: The sound heart contains nothing except love of God.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r5.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : السليم الذي لا يكون فيه إلا حبه

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r6.claim: One view defines the sound heart as free of worldly afflictions and afterlife attachments, with its concern fixed on its Master.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : السليم الذي قد سلم من آفات الدنيا ، ومطابع العقبى

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r7.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r7.claim: A sound heart is empty of afflictions and has not tasted the bitterness endured by those burdened with ailments.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r7.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : قلب سليم فارغ من الآفات لم يتجرع الغصص

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r8.claim: The sound-hearted person meets God with no aim except Him.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : الذي يلقى الله وليس له همة سواه

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r9.claim: The sound-hearted person enters life free of signs of wretchedness, avoids passion, leaves without an evil decree, and stands before God free of affliction and with God pleased.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم : السليم الذي يدخل الدنيا سالما من علامات الشقاء ، ويعيش في الدنيا سالما

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r10.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r10.claim: A sound heart is sound from everything besides God.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : قلب سليم أي : سليم من غير الله

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r11.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r11.claim: The sound heart is untouched by the afflictions of created existence and is empty of passing thoughts and inspirations.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r11.anchor: وقال أيضا : السليم الذي لا يشوبه شيء من آفات الكون الفارغ من الهواجس والموارد

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r12.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r12.claim: Abraham was tested in himself, family, and son, yet nothing affected him because his heart was soundly detached from created things; when his state with God was sound, everything else became insignificant.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r12.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : ابتلى إبراهيم عليه السلام في نفسه واهله ، وولده فلم يؤثر فيه شيء

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r13.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r13.claim: A sound heart meets God with no partner—unbelief, ostentation, or anything else—and is annihilated from things through God, then from God through God.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r13.anchor: وقال أيضا : القلب السليم هو أن يلقى الله ، وليس فيه من الله شريك من كفر أو رياء

SULAMI:v2p78#2/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r14.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r14.claim: An unnamed authority traces heart-soundness through certainty of scripture, gnosis, witnessing, and finally annihilation from states and forms; its sign is contentment in every state without inward opposition to God.
SULAMI:v2p78#2/r14.anchor: وسئل بعضهم : بما تنال سلامة الصدر ؟ قال : بالوقوف على حق اليقين وهو القرآن

SULAMI:v2p79/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p79/r1.claim: Abu Uthman gives four levels of a sound heart: freedom from shirk, active desires, ostentation and self-admiration, and remembrance of anything besides God.
SULAMI:v2p79/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : هو على أربع منازل : اولها : سلامة القلب من الشرك ، الثاني : سلامة القلب من الأهواء

SULAMI:v2p79/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p79/r2.claim: Kharrāz says the heart contains only God; citing Abraham's and Joseph's prayers to be Muslims, he defines Islam as sincere monotheism, humble servanthood, and continual conformity to God.
SULAMI:v2p79/r2.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخراز : في قوله : ﴿ إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم ﴾ قال ليس فيه إلا الله

SULAMI:v2p79/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r3.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p79/r3.claim: Qasim defines the sound heart as one protected from an evil decree.
SULAMI:v2p79/r3.anchor: قال القاسم : السليم الذي سلم من سوء القضاء

SULAMI:v2p79/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p79/r4.claim: An anonymous view defines it as a heart free of major sins.

SULAMI:v2p79/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r5.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p79/r5.claim: Another anonymous view defines it as a heart free of shirk.

SULAMI:v2p79/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r6.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p79/r6.claim: A further anonymous view defines it as free of hatred toward the Prophet's Companions.
SULAMI:v2p79/r6.anchor: وقيل : الذي سلم من بغض أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

SULAMI:v2p79/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r7.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p79/r7.claim: Sahl defines the sound heart as one free from innovations.
SULAMI:v2p79/r7.anchor: وقال سهل : الذي سلم من البدع

SULAMI:v2p79/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r8.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v2p79/r8.claim: Shibli defines it as sound and free of everything in the cosmos.
SULAMI:v2p79/r8.anchor: وقال الشبلي : سليما من جميع ما في الكون

SULAMI:v2p79/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r9.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
SULAMI:v2p79/r9.claim: Al-Warraq defines the sound heart as content with the course of God's decree in both what is loved and what is disliked.
SULAMI:v2p79/r9.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : القلب السليم الراضي لمجارى المقدور عليه في المحبوب والمكروه

SULAMI:v2p79/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r10.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p79/r10.claim: Sahl defines it as entrusting matters to God and being content with God's decree.
SULAMI:v2p79/r10.anchor: سمعت عبد الله الرازي يقول : سئل سهل عن قوله تعالى : ﴿ إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم ﴾ قال التفويض إلى الله

SULAMI:v2p79/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p79/r11.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p79/r11.claim: Ibn Tahir assigns Adam self-reproach and forgiveness, Abraham soundness and intimacy, and Muhammad steadfastness and love; he calls steadfastness in nearness and witnessing the highest character.
SULAMI:v2p79/r11.anchor: سمعت محمد بن عبد الله الرازي يقول : سمعت أبا بكر بن طاهر يقول : لكل نبي مع الله حال ومقام ، فمقام آدم الملامة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r2.claim: A sound heart is free of illness that alters its original God-given nature: Islam, headed by monotheism, upright good action, and adherence to the Sunna.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r2.anchor: عن افطرة الأولى التي فطره الله عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r3.claim: The exception is grammatically an unexpressed exception after the negation; wealth and children benefit the sound-hearted through good use of them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p371/r3.anchor: والاستثناء مفرغ , والظاهر أن قوله { وأزلقت } أي قربت بأيسر وجه

TUSTARI:26:89/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:26:89/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:26:89/r1.claim: A sound heart is free of innovations, entrusts its affair to God, and is content with God's decree.
TUSTARI:26:89/r1.anchor: الذي سلم من البدع مفوض إلى الله أمره راض بقدر الله

DURR-FULL:v6p307/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r1.claim: A report describes Abraham's unbelieving father as transformed into a filthy beast and cast into Hell; the following Prophetic report names the father as Āzar and recounts Abraham's appeal not to be shamed by his fate.
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r1.anchor: وأخرج البخاري والنسائي عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يلقى إبراهيم أباه آزر يوم القيامة وعلى وجه آزر قترة وغبرة

DURR-FULL:v6p307/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the sound heart as testifying that there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} قال: شهداة أن لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v6p307/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r4.claim: Qatāda transmits the gloss that a sound heart is free from polytheism.
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} قال: كان يقال: سليم من الشرك

DURR-FULL:v6p307/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the heart is free of polytheism and has no doubt about the truth.
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r5.anchor:
عن مجاهد في قوله {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} قال: من الشرك
ليس فيه شك في الحق

DURR-FULL:v6p307/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r6.speaker: عون
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r6.claim: ʿAwn recounts Ibn Sīrīn's concern that al-Ḥajjāj's gravest danger was not his sins but whether he would meet God with a sound heart, which he defines as knowing there is no god but God.
DURR-FULL:v6p307/r6.anchor: عن عون قال: ذكروا الحجاج عند ابن سيرين فقال: غير ما تقولون أخوف على الحجاج عندي منه

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains a sound heart as affirming that there is no god but God.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء ، عن ابن عباس الا من اتى الله بقلب سليم قال شهادة ان لا اله الا الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r2.claim: Ibn Sirin says the sound heart knows God is true, the Hour is coming, and God will resurrect those in the graves.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r2.anchor: عن عوف قال : قلت لمحمد بن سيرين : ما القلب السليم قال : يعلم بان الله حق وان الساعة قائمة وان الله يبعث من في القبور

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r3.claim: Mujahid first defines the sound heart as being free of associating partners with God.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد الا من اتى الله بقلب سليم سليم من الشرك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r4.claim: Mujahid also describes the sound heart as having no doubt about the truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد بقلب سليم ليس فيه شك في الحق

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r5.claim: Al-Hasan likewise defines the sound heart as free of associating partners with God.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r5.anchor: عن جسر ، عن الحسن في قوله : الا من اتى الله بقلب سليم قال : سليم من الشرك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r6.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says the sound heart is free of shirk, while no one is free of sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r6.anchor: سمعت عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قوله : الا من اتى الله بقلب سليم قال : سليم من الشرك فاما الذنوب فليس يسلم منها أحد

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the sound heart as sincere and devoted.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك بقلب سليم قال : مخلص

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r8.speaker: أبوه
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r8.claim: Hisham's father interprets a sound heart as one that does not curse.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r8.anchor: عن هشام ، عن أبيه الا من اتى الله بقلب سليم قال الا يكون لعانا

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak also describes the sound-hearted person as sincere toward God among His creatures.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2783#2/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك الا من اتى الله بقلب سليم قال : الناصح لله في خلقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r4.claim: After a final call to the true religion and a request for forgiveness, Ibrahim turns to supplications gathering spiritual perfection through prophethood and calling people to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r4.anchor: لما كان آخر مقاله في الدعوة إلى الدين الحق متضمنا دعاء بطلب المغفرة تخلص منه إلى الدعاء بما فيه جمع الكمال النفساني بالرسالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r1.claim: Priority in good deeds is prized: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ said he was first to shoot an arrow in God’s cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r1.anchor: قال سعد بن أبي وقاص ( أنا أول من رمى بسهم في سبيل الله ) .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r2.claim: A hadith says Adam’s first son bears a share of every unjust killing because he first established the practice; the author gives no grading here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r2.anchor: ففي الحديث : ( ما من نفس تقتل ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول كفل من دمها ذلك لأنه أول من سن القتل )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r3.claim: Ibrahim’s five requests for spiritual gifts answer the five bodily gifts described earlier; forgiveness for his father is inserted within his plea not to be shamed on Resurrection Day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p145/r3.anchor: وقد قابل إبراهيم في دعائه النعم الخمس التي أنعم الله بها عليه المذكورة في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r1.claim: The exception is from the object of ينفع, not its subject: the person arriving with a sound heart is benefited, not a benefactor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r1.anchor: والمستثنى وهو { من أتى الله بقلب سليم } متعين لأن يكون استثناء من مفعول { ينفع } وليس مستثنى من فاعل { ينفع }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r2.claim: The construction implies an omitted general benefactor, while the sound heart is the cause of benefit and thus one instance of that implied subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r2.anchor: ويبين إجماله متعلق فعل { ينفع } وهو { بقلب سليم } إذ كان القلب السليم سبب النفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r3.claim: The person is both benefited and self-benefiting in different respects, a rhetorical abstraction in which the heart causes the person’s benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r3.anchor: فصار ذلك الشخص نافعا ومنفوعا باختلاف الاعتبار ، وهو ضرب من التجريد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r4.claim: The exception is connected and emptied of the object; treating it as disconnected does not resolve the grammatical difficulty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r4.anchor: ولهذا فالاستثناء متصل مفرغ عن المفعول . وقد حصل من نسج الكلام على هذا المنوال إيجاز مغنن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r5.claim: The heart is inner cognition, while soundness means strong moral health: freedom from beliefs in shirk and psychological purification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r5.anchor: والقلب : الإدراك الباطني . والسليم : الموصوف بقوة السلامة ، والمراد بها هنا السلامة المعنوية المجازية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r6.claim: The metaphorical opposite of a sound heart is a sick heart, as in the verse saying there is sickness in their hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r6.anchor: وضده المريض مرضا مجازيا قال تعالى : { في قلوبهم مرض } ( البقرة : 10 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r7.claim: Only inward soundness is mentioned because it grounds outward righteous action; its status is judged by the final state, when people arrive with sound hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p149/r7.anchor: والاقتصار على السليم هنا لأن السلامة باعث الأعمال الصالحة الظاهرية

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p318/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p318/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p318/r1.claim: A sound heart is one free from associationism.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.claim: A sound heart is free of association and sins, and relinquishes worldly attachments even when lawful, such as wealth and children.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r3.anchor: خالص من الشرك والمعاصي، وعلق الدنيا المتروكة وإن كانت مباحة كالمال والبنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.speaker: سفيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.claim: Sufyan defines the sound heart as meeting God with nothing else in one’s heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r4.anchor: قال سفيان هو الذي يلقى ربه وليس في قلبه شيء غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.claim: The wording supports a general meaning, though freedom from association is the most important sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا يقتضي عموم اللفظة، ولكن السليم من الشرك هو الأهم، وقال الجنيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.speaker: الجنيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.claim: Junayd describes it as a heart stung by fear of God, explaining salīm as ladīgh, “stung.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p235#2/r6.anchor: بقلب لديغ من خشية الله والسليم اللديغ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.claim: Abraham argues that divinity belongs only to the one who performs these acts of creation, guidance, provision, healing, and forgiveness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#5/r4.anchor: وهذا احتجاج على قومه أنه لا تصلح الإلهية إلا لمن فعل هذه الأفعال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r1.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r1.claim: Hasan and Ibn Zayd say a sound heart is free of associating partners with God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r1.anchor: سليم من الشرك قاله الحسن وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r2.claim: Mujahid says a sound heart is free of doubt.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r3.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib says it is the healthy heart of a believer, unlike the diseased hearts of disbelievers and hypocrites.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r3.anchor: سليم أي صحيح وهو قلب المؤمن لان قلب الكافر والمنافق مريض قاله سعيد بن المسيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r4.speaker: الجنيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r4.claim: Junayd connects the word linguistically with one bitten by a snake: the heart is like one stung by fear of God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r4.anchor: أن السليم في اللغة اللديغ فالمعنى كاللديغ من خوف الله تعالى قاله الجنيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r5.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r5.claim: Husayn ibn al-Fadl says it is free from the afflictions of wealth and children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r5.anchor: سليم من آفات المال والبنين قاله الحسين بن الفضل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r6.claim: Al-Tha'labi transmits that it is free of innovation and settled in the Sunnah.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p130#5/r6.anchor: سليم من البدعة مطمئن على السنة حكاه الثعلبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r6.claim: Only faith, sincere devotion, and renunciation of shirk benefit on that Day; a sound heart is free of stain and polytheism.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r6.anchor: ولا ينفع يومئذ إلا الإيمان بالله، وإخلاص الدين له، والتبري من الشرك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r7.claim: A sound heart is free from stain and shirk.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r8.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r8.claim: Ibn Sirin defines a sound heart as knowing God is true, the Hour is certainly coming, and God will raise those in the graves.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن سيرين: القلب السليم أن يعلم أن الله حق، وأن الساعة آتية لا ريب فيها، وأن الله يبعث من في القبور.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says a sound heart is alive and attests that there is no god but God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} حيي (5) يشهد أن لا إله إلا الله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r10.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r10.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan explain a sound heart as one free from shirk.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r10.anchor: قال مجاهد، والحسن، وغيرهما: {بقلب سليم} يعني: من الشرك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r11.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib calls the sound heart a healthy believer's heart; unbelievers' and hypocrites' hearts are diseased.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r11.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: القلب السليم: هو القلب الصحيح، وهو قلب المؤمن؛ لأن قلب [الكافر و] (6) المنافق مريض، قال الله: {في قلوبهم مرض} [البقرة:10]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r12.speaker: أبو عثمان النيسابوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r12.claim: Abu Uthman al-Naysaburi defines a sound heart as free of innovation and settled in the Sunnah.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p149/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان النيسابوري: هو القلب الخالي من البدعة، المطمئن إلى السنة.

MUQATIL:26:86-89/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:86-89/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:86-89/r4.claim: Only one who comes to God sincere in monotheism, free of shirk, benefits on resurrection; wealth and offspring then benefit him.
MUQATIL:26:86-89/r4.anchor: فى الآخرة { بقلب سليم } [آية: 89] من الشرك مخلصا لله عز وجل بالتوحيد،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r1.claim: A sound heart is free of disbelief and hypocrisy; the disbeliever’s and hypocrite’s hearts are diseased, as 2:10 says.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r1.anchor: عن الكفر والنفاق فقلب الكافر والمنافق مريض لقوله تعالى فى قلوبهم مرض

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r2.claim: Wealth and sons can benefit when wealth is spent in good causes and the sons are righteous, alongside a sound heart.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r2.anchor: أن المال إذا صرف فى وجوه البر وبنوه صالحون فانه ينتفع به وبهم سليم القلب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r3.claim: Alternatively, wealth and sons signify riches: the only enduring richness is the sound heart brought to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r3.anchor: أو جعل المال والبنون فى معنى الغنى كأنه قيل يوم لا ينفع غنى الا غنى من أتى الله بقلب سليم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r4.claim: Grammatically, من is the object of ينفع: only a person whose heart guides use of wealth and care of sons benefits.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r4.anchor: وقد جعل من مفعولا لينفع أى لا ينفع مال ولا بنون إلا رجلا قلبه مع ماله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r5.claim: The sound-hearted person spends wealth in obedience and guides his sons in religion, teaching them the religious laws.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r5.anchor: حيث أرشدهم إلى الدين وعلمهم الشرائع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r6.claim: God honors Abraham by confirming the exception for him and making the sound heart an attribute of Abraham (37:83–84).
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r6.anchor: ثم جعله صفة له فى قوله وأن من شيعته لابراهيم إذ جاء ربه بقلب سليم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r7.claim: Ibrahim begins with a settled rhetorical question about worship, then refutes idols as unable to harm, benefit, or hear.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r7.anchor: حيث سألهم أولا عما يعبدون سؤال مقرر لا مستفهم ثم أقبل على آلهتهم فابطل امرها بأنها لا تضر ولا تنفع ولا تسمع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r8.claim: Ibrahim shows that ancestral imitation is not even a doubt, much less a proof.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r8.anchor: وعلى تقليدهم آباءهم الاقدمين فاخرجه من أن يكون شبهة فضلا عن أن يكون حجة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r9.claim: He stages the issue within himself, then turns to mention God, magnifies Him, and recounts His favors from creation through death and hoped-for mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r9.anchor: ثم صور المسألة فى نفسه دونهم حتى تخلص منها إلى ذكر الله تعالى فعظم شأنه وعدد نعمته من حين إنشائه إلى وقت وفاته

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r10.claim: Ibrahim follows with sincere supplications and a decorous appeal, then resurrection, reward and punishment, the polytheists’ remorse, and their wish to return and obey.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#10/r10.anchor: ثم اتبع ذلك أن دعا بدعوات المخلصين وابتهل اليه ابتهال الأدب ثم وصله بذكر يوم القيامة وثواب الله وعقابه

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r13.claim: One parsing makes the exception from the disbelievers: wealth and sons benefit no one except the person who comes to God with a sound heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r13.anchor: هو استثناء من الكافرين أي لا ينفعه ماله ولا بنوه.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r14.claim: Another parsing treats the exception as unlike its antecedent: the person with a sound heart does benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو استثناء من غير الجنس، أي لكن { من أتى الله بقلب سليم } ينفعه لسلامة قلبه.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r15.claim: The heart is singled out because soundness of heart makes the limbs sound, while its corruption corrupts the other limbs.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:84-89/r15.anchor: وخص القلب بالذكر لأنه الذي إذا سلم سلمت الجوارح، وإذا فسد فسدت سائر الجوارح.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r1.claim: Qurtubi cites the phrase about sickness in hearts as a related scriptural description of diseased hearts.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r1.anchor: في قلوبهم مرض [البقرة: 10] وقال أبو عثمان السياري:

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان السياري
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r2.claim: Abu Uthman al-Sayyari defines a sound heart as free from innovation and settled upon the Sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان السياري: هو القلب الخالي عن البدعة المطمئن إلى السنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r3.claim: Hasan says the sound heart is uninjured by wealth and children.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: سليم من آفة المال والبنين.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r4.speaker: الجنيد
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r4.claim: Junayd explains salim as literally one stung, so the heart is like one stung by fear of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r4.anchor: وقال الجنيد: السليم في اللغة اللديغ فمعناه أنه قلب كاللديغ من خوف الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r5.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the sound heart as sincere and pure.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r6.claim: Qurtubi prefers al-Dahhak's broad reading: a sound heart is pure of blameworthy traits and characterized by beautiful ones, gathering the other views.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r6.anchor: قلت: وهذا القول يجمع شتات الأقوال بعمومه وهو حسن، أي الخالص من الأوصاف الذميمة، والمتصف بالأوصاف الجميلة والله أعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r7.speaker: عروة
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r7.claim: Urwa tells his sons not to curse, saying Abraham never cursed anything and had a sound heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r7.anchor: وقد روي عن عروة أنه قال: يا بني لا تكونوا لعانين فإن إبراهيم لم يلعن شيئا قط،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r8.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r8.claim: Ibn Sirin says a sound heart knows God is true, the Hour is coming, and God will raise those in graves.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r8.anchor: وقال محمد بن سيرين: القلب السليم أن يعلم أن الله حق، وأن الساعة قائمة، وأن الله يبعث من في القبور.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in Sahih Muslim that people will enter Paradise with hearts like birds; Qurtubi takes the likeness as purity from sin and defect, perhaps with little worldly experience.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r9.anchor: " يدخل الجنة أقوام أفئدتهم مثل أفئدة الطير "

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r10.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying most people of Paradise are simple-minded; Qurtubi grades the hadith sound and means simple in avoiding God's disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r10.anchor: كما روى أنس بن مالك قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أكثر أهل الجنة البله " وهو حديث صحيح. أي البله عن معاصي الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r11.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r11.claim: Al-Azhari says these simple people are innately disposed to good and unaware of evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r11.anchor: قال الأزهري: الأبله هنا هو الذي طبع على الخير وهو غافل عن الشر لا يعرفه.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r12.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r12.claim: Al-Qutabi describes them as people dominated by sound hearts and good opinions of others.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:83-89/r12.anchor: وقال القتبي: البله هم الذين غلبت عليهم سلامة الصدور وحسن الظن بالناس.

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r4.claim: God honored Abraham with the description of a sound heart, also used of Abraham in 37:83–84.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r4.anchor: أكرمه بهذا الوصف حيث قال : { وإن من شيعته

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r5.claim: One parsing makes the exception a replacement: asked whether Zayd has wealth and sons, one answers that his wealth and sons are soundness of heart, denying the possessions and affirming the heart instead.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r5.anchor: تريد نفي المال والبنين عنه وإثبات سلامة القلب له

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r6.claim: A second parsing takes wealth and sons to mean worldly affluence: only the religious wealth of a person with a sound heart benefits, as worldly wealth consists in possessions and children.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r6.anchor: نجعل المال والبنين في معنى الغنى كأنه قيل يوم لا ينفع غنى إلا غنى من أتى الله بقلب سليم

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r7.claim: A third parsing makes the exception the object of benefits: wealth and sons help only a person whose heart is sound, who spends wealth in obedience and guides children to religion; the heart is also free from their temptation.

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r8.claim: The sound heart most correctly means freedom from ignorance and vile traits: just as bodily health is the proper constitution and illness its loss, the heart needs knowledge and excellent character and must be free of false beliefs and worldly desires.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r8.anchor: وهو الأصح أن المراد منه سلامة القلب عن الجهل والأخلاق الرذيلة

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r9.claim: An objection says that if a sound heart suffices for salvation, the tongue and limbs need no soundness; Razi answers that the heart governs and the limbs follow, so their failure proves the heart is unsound.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r9.anchor: أن القلب مؤثر واللسان والجوارح تبع فلو كان القلب سليما لكانا سليمين لا محالة

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r10.claim: A further interpretation says sound means bitten, in fear of God.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r10.anchor: أن السليم هو اللديغ من خشية الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r11.claim: Another interpretation understands sound as the one who is safe, submits, yields, and surrenders.
RAZI-FULL:v24p130/r11.anchor: أن السليم هو الذي سلم وأسلم وسالم واستسلم

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r1.claim: A sound heart is also associated with Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r1.anchor: A sound heart is also associated with Abraham

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r2.claim: Q says a sound heart knows that God is real, the Hereafter will come, and God will resurrect the dead in their graves.
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r2.anchor: it refers to knowing that God is real, that the Hereafter will come, and that God will resurrect what is in the graves (Q)

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r3.claim: Ṭ says a sound heart is free of doubts and sincere.
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r3.anchor: a heart without doubts and one that is sincere (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r4.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r4.claim: IK says a sound heart is free of polytheism.

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r5.claim: R says a sound heart is free of ignorance, vices, and attachments to worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r5.anchor: ignorance, vices, and attachments to the life of this world (R)

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r6.speaker: Th
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r6.claim: Th describes it as a spiritually healthy heart rather than a sick one.
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r6.anchor: the heart that is spiritually healthy as opposed to one that is sick (Th)

STUDYQURAN:26:89/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r7.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r7.claim: Su describes the sound heart as empty of all but its Lord and happy only with Him.
STUDYQURAN:26:89/r7.anchor: a heart that is empty of all but its Lord and only happy with Him (Su)

TAB-FULL:v17p596/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r1.speaker: محمد
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r1.claim: Muḥammad defines a sound heart as certainty that God is real, the Hour will come, and God will raise those in the graves.
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r1.anchor: قلت لمحمد: " ما القلب السليم؟ قال: أن يعلم أن الله حق، وأن الساعة قائمة، وأن الله يبعث من في القبور "

TAB-FULL:v17p596/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r2.claim: Mujahid says a sound heart contains no doubt about the truth.
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} [الشعراء: 89] قال: لا شك فيه "

TAB-FULL:v17p596/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets a sound heart as free of associating partners with God.
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {بقلب سليم} [الشعراء: 89] قال: «سليم من الشرك»

TAB-FULL:v17p596/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says a sound heart is free of shirk, while noting that no one is free from sins.
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد: {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} [الشعراء: 89] قال: «سليم من الشرك، فأما الذنوب فليس يسلم منها أحد»

TAB-FULL:v17p596/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses a sound heart as sincere or pure.
TAB-FULL:v17p596/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قول الله: " {إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم} [الشعراء: 89] قال: هو الخالص "

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r1.claim: A disconnected exception means rather the person arriving with a sound heart benefits; the author presents al-Zamakhsharī's required ellipsis of a state of soundness.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r1.anchor: فيه أوجه، أحدها: أنه منقطع أي: لكن من أتى الله بقلب سليم فإنه ينفعه ذلك. وقال الزمخشري: " ولا بد لك مع ذلك من تقدير مضاف

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says an omitted state of soundness must be supplied because soundness is not of the same kind as wealth and children.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " ولا بد لك مع ذلك من تقدير مضاف وهو الحال المراد بها السلامة، وليست من جنس المال والبنين،

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r3.claim: The Shaykh denies that omitting an implied noun is necessary.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا ضرورة تدعو إلى حذف المضاف كما ذكر ".

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r4.claim: The author defends the implied state because it lets the exception be understood as included in what is excepted from; otherwise the construction fails, as with horses neighing except camels.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r4.anchor: قلت: إنما قدر المضاف ليتوهم دخول المستثنى في المستثنى منه؛ لأنه متى لم يتوهم ذلك لم يقع الاستثناء، ولهذا منعوا: " صهلت الخيل إلا الإبل "

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r5.claim: Another parse makes the person an object of yanfaʿ: his charitable spending and righteous children benefit him.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r5.anchor: الثاني: أنه مفعول به لقوله: " لا ينفع " أي: لا ينفع المال والبنون إلا هذا الشخص فإنه ينفعه

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r6.claim: Another parse makes the person a substitute for an omitted object or the excluded person: no wealth or children benefit anyone except one of this description.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r6.anchor: الثالث: أنه بدل من المفعول المحذوف، أو مستثنى منه، إذ التقدير: لا ينفع مال ولا بنون أحدا من الناس إلا من كانت هذه صفته.

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r7.claim: The omitted excluded noun is supported by a poetic line meaning no one escaped by anything except a sword's sheath and a loincloth.

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ parses the exception as a substitute for the subject of yanfaʿ, with rational beings predominating: a person's wealth or children benefit him and others through intercession.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r8.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وغلب من يعقل فيكون التقدير: إلا مال من، أو بنو من فإنه ينفع نفسه وغيره بالشفاعة ".

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r9.claim: The author says Abu al-Baqāʾ has conflated two distinct ways to parse a subject substitute.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r9.anchor: قلت: وأبو البقاء خلط وجها بوجه: وذلك أنه إذا أردنا أن نجعله بدلا من فاعل " ينفع " فلنا فيه طريقان

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r10.claim: One subject-substitute route uses predominance: children prevail over wealth, so the exception is a righteous child who benefits himself and others.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r10.anchor: أحدهما: طريقة التغليب أي: غلبنا البنين على المال، فاستثنى من البنين،

SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r11.claim: The other route supplies a possessive noun before man, yielding someone's wealth or someone's children.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89/r11.anchor: والطريقة الثانية: أن تقدر مضافا محذوفا قبل " من " أي: إلا مال من أو بنو من

SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r1.claim: Continuing al-Zamakhsharī's connected-exception analysis, one reading treats the exception as the state of the person who comes to God with a sound heart, following the cited poetic pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r1.anchor:
تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع
" وما ثوابه إلا السيف " ومثاله أن يقال:

SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's second connected reading treats wealth and children as worldly riches and a sound heart as a person's religious riches.
SAMIN-DURR:26:89#2/r2.anchor: والثاني قال: " وإن شئت حملت الكلام على المعنى وجعلت المال والبنين في معنى الغنى، كأنه قيل: يوم لا ينفع غنى إلا غنى من أتى،

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r5.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines soundness and safety as being free of outward and inward afflictions.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r5.anchor: قال الراغب السلم والسلامة التعري من الآفات الظاهرة والباطنة

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r6.claim: The exception is disconnected: it states what does benefit at Resurrection, namely a sound heart, whether its owner had worldly wealth and children or not.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r6.anchor: فالاستثناء منقطع، والمعنى لكن من أتى الله بقلب سليم فإنه ينتفع به

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r7.claim: One reported connected reading supplies the omitted object of benefit: no wealth or children benefit anyone except the person who comes with a sound heart.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r7.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء متصل والمستثنى منه مفعول ينفع المحذوف والتقدير يوم لا ينفع مال ولا بنون أحدا

TABATABAI:26:88-89/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r8.claim: A second reported connected reading supplies an omitted possessive phrase: only the wealth and children belonging to the person with a sound heart benefit.
TABATABAI:26:88-89/r8.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء متصل والكلام بتقدير مضاف، والتقدير لا ينفع مال ولا بنون إلا مال وبنوه

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r1.claim: A third connected proposal reads wealth and children as affluence and supplies an omitted noun: only the affluence of a sound-hearted person benefits; calling the heart's soundness affluence makes the connection figurative.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r1.anchor: وقيل المال والبنون في معنى الغنى والاستثناء منه بحذف مضاف من نوعه والتقدير يوم لا ينفع غنى

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r2.claim: A fourth proposal keeps the exception disconnected but supplies an omitted word for the state of the person who comes with a sound heart.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r2.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء منقطع وهناك مضاف محذوف، والتقدير لا ينفع مال ولا بنون إلا حال من أتى

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r3.claim: The three connected readings restrict the distinction to wealthy parents and leave the poor and childless unaddressed, against the context; the fourth requires an unnecessary ellipsis.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r3.anchor: والأقوال الثلاثة الأول توجب اختصاص تميز اليوم بمن له مال وبنون فقط

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r4.claim: The sound heart means a soul free of the stain of wrongdoing, namely polytheism and disobedience.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r4.anchor: وهو النفس السالمة من وصمه الظلم وهو الشرك والمعصية

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r5.claim: The verse is close in meaning to the description of wealth and children as worldly adornment, while lasting good deeds are better with God; here benefit is assigned to the sound heart.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r5.anchor: الآية قريبة المعنى من قوله تعالى المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا والباقيات الصالحات خير عند ربك

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r6.claim: The humbled faces and failure of those bearing wrongdoing on that Day support reading a sound heart as one free from injustice.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r6.anchor: وعنت الوجوه للحي القيوم وقد خاب من حمل ظلما طه 111

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r7.claim: One commentator argues these verses show Abraham sought his father's guidance to faith, since he could not knowingly seek posthumous forgiveness for an unbeliever through intercession; the author's response is that this depends on a connected exception and the rejected claim that Azar was Abraham's biological father.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r7.anchor: قال بعضهم وفي الآيتين تأييد لكون استغفاره عليه السلام لأبيه طلبا لهدايته إلى الإيمان

TABATABAI:26:89-91/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r8.claim: With a disconnected exception, the sound-heart verse together with the rule that intercession is only for those God approves shows Abraham prayed before his father's death.
TABATABAI:26:89-91/r8.anchor: وأما إذا أخذ الاستثناء منقطعا فقوله { إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم } بضميمة قوله تعالى ولا يشفعون إلا لمن ارتضى

TABATABAI:26:69-104/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r4.speaker: المسؤول
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r4.claim: A report in al-Kafi says a sound heart meets God with no one but Him; any heart containing polytheism or doubt is ruined, and renunciation of worldly life empties hearts for the Hereafter.
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r4.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن سفيان بن عيينة قال سألته عن قول الله عز وجل { إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم }

TABATABAI:26:69-104/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r5.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r5.claim: A report in al-Majma' defines the sound heart as one free from love of this world; the author notes support in the Prophetic saying that love of the world is the root of every sin.
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r5.anchor: وفي المجمع وروي عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال هو القلب الذي سلم من حب الدنيا

TABATABAI:26:69-104/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:26:69-104/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that love of worldly life is the root of every sin, supporting the reported definition of a sound heart as free of worldly attachment.

TABRISI:26:85-89/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:85-89/r6.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
TABRISI:26:85-89/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid define a sound heart as free from associating partners with God and from doubt.
TABRISI:26:85-89/r6.anchor: من الشرك والشك عن الحسن ومجاهد.

TABRISI:26:85-89/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:85-89/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:26:85-89/r7.claim: Another interpretation is a heart free from corruption and sins.

TABRISI:26:85-89/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:85-89/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:85-89/r8.claim: The heart is singled out because a sound heart keeps the limbs sound; bodily corruption follows only from corrupt intention in the heart.
TABRISI:26:85-89/r8.anchor: وإنما خص القلب بالسلامة لأنه إذا سلم القلب سلم سائر الجوارح من الفساد

TABRISI:26:85-89/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:85-89/r9.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:26:85-89/r9.claim: Al-Ṣādiq defines a sound heart as free from love of the world and supports this with the Prophetic saying that worldly love is the root of every sin.
TABRISI:26:85-89/r9.anchor:
وروي عن الصادق ع أنه قال هو القلب الذي سلم من حب الدنيا ويؤيده قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" حب الدنيا رأس كل خطيئة

THALABI:v7p171/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p171/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v7p171/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says a sound heart is healthy: a believer’s heart is healthy, while a disbeliever’s or hypocrite’s is sick, as another verse says.
THALABI:v7p171/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: القلب السليم هو الصحيح، وهو قلب المؤمن لأن قلب الكافر والمنافق مريض

THALABI:v7p171/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p171/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان النيسابوري
THALABI:v7p171/r3.claim: Abu ʿUthman al-Nisaburi defines the sound heart as free of innovation and settled in the Sunna.
THALABI:v7p171/r3.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان النيسابوري: هو القلب الخالي من البدعة، المطمئن على السنة

THALABI:v7p171/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p171/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v7p171/r4.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says it is free of the affliction of wealth and children.
THALABI:v7p171/r4.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: سليم من آفة المال والبنين

THALABI:v7p171/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p171/r5.speaker: الجنيد
THALABI:v7p171/r5.claim: Al-Junayd notes that “salim” can mean bitten, so the sound heart is like one bitten by fear of God.
THALABI:v7p171/r5.anchor: وقال الجنيد: السليم في اللغة اللديغ فمعناه: كاللديغ من خوف الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r1.claim: One reading makes the exception part of the preceding statement: an unbeliever's wealth, even if given in charity, and sons cannot help him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: إنه استثناء من الأول على معنى: أن الكافر لا ينفعه ماله وإن تصدق به، ولا ابنوه يغيثونه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r2.claim: A second reading takes the exception as separate: the soundness of the heart benefits the person who comes to God with it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r2.anchor: لكن من أتى الله بقلب سليم ينفعه ذلك، وهو سلامة قلبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الكلبي، مقاتل، قتادة، الحسن، وأكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r3.claim: They define a sound heart as free from shirk, doubt, and hypocrisy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: سليم من الشرك والنفاق. وهو قول مجاهد، والكلبي، ومقاتل، وقتادة، والحسن، وأكثر المفسرين؛ قالوا: القلب السليم، الذي سلم من الشرك، والشك، والنفاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r4.claim: A heart free of these faults is certain in faith and sincere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r4.anchor: وإذا كان سليما من هذه الأشياء كان موقنا مخلصا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r5.claim: He says a sound heart is a healthy heart: the believer's is healthy, while the unbeliever's and hypocrite's are sick, as in 2:10.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p75#2/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد # ابن المسيب: القلب السليم هو الصحيح وهو قلب المؤمن، وقلب الكافر والمنافق مريض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:89-91/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:89-91/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:89-91/r1.claim: The sound heart is one free of associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:26:89-91/r1.anchor: إلا من أتى الله بقلب سليم } سلم من الشرك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.claim: Qatāda, as transmitted by Saʿīd, says the sound heart is free of associationism.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p510/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: أي: من الشرك، في تفسير سعيد، عن قتادة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r1.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes the verbs: atā is an arrival made easily, whereas jāʾa is broader because atā is only an easy kind of coming.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r1.anchor: قال الراغب الأصفهاني مفرقاً بين الإتيان والمجيء: "الإتيان مجيءٌ بسهولة، ومنه قيل للسيل المار على وجهه أتي"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r2.claim: The lexicographers do not state al-Rāghib's distinction; they generally define jāʾa through atā and atā through jāʾa.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r2.anchor: ولم يذكر أهل المعجمات ما ذكره الراغب، وإنما هم يفسرون واحداً بالآخر، فيفسرون جاء بأتى، وأتى بجاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r3.claim: Some derivatives of atā nevertheless signal ease, as in a well-traveled path and in making channels or a stream's route easy; he uses this usage to support al-Rāghib's distinction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r3.anchor: يقولون مثلاً في تفسير الطريق الميتاء من (أتى) "طريق مسلوك يسلكه كل أحد" وذلك لسهولته ويسره

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r4.claim: He infers that the Qurʾān uses jāʾa for difficult or strenuous arrivals, or for things harder than those expressed with atā, citing grave events and acts of wrongdoing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p97/r4.anchor: والذي استبان لي أن القرآن الكريم، يستعملُ المجيءَ لما فيه صعوبةٌ ومشقة، أو لما هو صعب وأشق مما تُستعمل له (أتى)

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r17.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r17.claim: Mujahid defines a sound heart as free from doubt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r17.anchor: أحدها : سليم من الشك , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r18.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r18.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd define a sound heart as free from associating partners with God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r18.anchor: الثاني : سليم من الشرك , قاله الحسن , وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r19.claim: A sound heart may mean freedom from sins, since soundness of the heart brings soundness of the limbs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r19.anchor: الثالث : من المعاصي , لأنه إذا سلم القلب سلمت الجوارح

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r20.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r20.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses a sound heart as sincere or pure.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r21.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي حاتم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r21.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim describes it as sincere toward people in one’s conduct.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r21.anchor: الخامس : أنه الناصح في خلقه , قاله عبد الرحمن بن أبي حاتم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r22.claim: Al-Mawardi also suggests a heart free of fear at resurrection because of the preceding glad tidings at the moment of seeing God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p176/r22.anchor: سليم القلب من الخوف في القيامة لما تقدم من البشرى عند المعاينة

QASHANI:26:83-84/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:26:83-84/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:26:83-84/r3.claim: A sound heart is free both of deficiency in its original aptitude and of the veils of the soul's attributes in embodied life.
QASHANI:26:83-84/r3.anchor: وسلامة القلب بأمرين: براءته عن نقص الاستعداد في الفطرة، ونزاهته عن حجب صفات النفس في النشأة

BURHAN:v1p266/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
BURHAN:v1p266/r1.claim: One lexical meaning of āya is a group: Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī cites the expression “the people went out with their āya,” meaning their group.
BURHAN:v1p266/r1.anchor: أحدها جماعة الحروف قال أبو عمرو الشيباني تقول العرب خرج القوم بآيتهم أي بجماعتهم

BURHAN:v1p266/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r2.speaker: شاعر
BURHAN:v1p266/r2.claim: Āya can also mean a marvel; the cited poet calls someone a wonder in beauty with no equal.
BURHAN:v1p266/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر … آية فى الجمال ليس له فى ال … حسن شبه وما له من نظير

BURHAN:v1p266/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r3.speaker: العرب
BURHAN:v1p266/r3.claim: Āya can mean a sign or trace, as in saying that no sign remained in a ruined house; each Qur’anic verse is a sign of Muhammad’s prophethood.
BURHAN:v1p266/r3.anchor: ثالثها العلامة تقول العرب خربت دار فلان وما بقى فيها آية أي علامة فكأن كل آية في القرآن علامة ودلالة على نبوة محمد

BURHAN:v1p266/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r4.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v1p266/r4.claim: Sībawayh derives āya from ayya, on the faʿla pattern: the yāʾ moves and the preceding vowel opens to produce āya.
BURHAN:v1p266/r4.anchor: فقال سيبويه فعلة بفتح العين وأصلها أيية

BURHAN:v1p266/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r5.speaker: الكسائي
BURHAN:v1p266/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī derives āya from āyiyah and says the first yāʾ was deleted to avoid the gemination seen in dābbah.
BURHAN:v1p266/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي أصلها آيية على وزن فاعلة حذفت الياء الأولى مخافة أن يلتزم فيها من الإدغام ما لزم في دابة

BURHAN:v1p266/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r6.speaker: الجعبرى
BURHAN:v1p266/r6.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī defines an āya technically as a Qur’anic unit made of clauses, actually or by estimation, with a beginning and end within a sūra; the name derives from sign or group.
BURHAN:v1p266/r6.anchor: فقال الجعبرى فى كتاب المفرد فى معرفة العدد حد الآية قرآن مركب

BURHAN:v1p266/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r7.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v1p266/r7.claim: Another definition is a portion of Qur’an separated from what precedes and follows it, with no counterpart elsewhere.
BURHAN:v1p266/r7.anchor: وقال غيره الآية طائفة من القرآن منقطعة عما قبلها وما بعدها ليس بينها شبه بما سواها

BURHAN:v1p266/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r8.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v1p266/r8.claim: Another view defines an āya as one of the counted units in a sūra, named for proving the messenger’s truth and challengers’ inability.
BURHAN:v1p266/r8.anchor: وقيل هي الواحدة من المعدودات في السور سميت به لأنها علامة على صدق من أتى بها وعلى عجز المتحدي بها

BURHAN:v1p266/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r9.speaker: الواحدي وبعض أصحابنا
BURHAN:v1p266/r9.claim: A further view says an āya marks the interruption of one passage from another; al-Wāḥidī and colleagues note that this could imply calling a shorter unit an āya, were its present limits not fixed by transmission.
BURHAN:v1p266/r9.anchor: قال الواحدى وبعض أصحابنا يجوز على هذا القول تسمية أقل من الآية آية لولا أن التوقيف ورد بما هي عليه الآن

BURHAN:v1p266/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p266/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v1p266/r11.claim: Some hold that verse boundaries, like sūra boundaries, are known only through prophetic instruction, defining an āya as a transmitted group of letters set apart in meaning from its surroundings.
BURHAN:v1p266/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم الصحيح أنها إنما تعلم بتوقيف من الشارع لا مجال للقياس فيه كمعرفة السورة فالآية طائفة حروف من القرآن علم بالتوقيف انقطاعها معنى
